passages.title: The biotic community
passages.body:
Directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the items based on it. You are required to select your answers based solely on the contents of the passage and the opinion of the author.

The grouping or assemblage of plants, animals and microbes we observe when we study a natural forest, a grassland, a pond, a coral reef or some other undisturbed area, is referred to as the area's biota or biotic community. The plant portion of the biotic community includes all vegetation, from large trees down through to microscopic algae. Likewise, the animal portion includes everything from large mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians through to earthworms, tiny insects and mites. Microbes encompass a large array of microscopic bacteria, fungi and protozoans. Thus, the biotic community comprises a plant community, an animal community and a microbial community.

The particular kind of biotic community found in a given area is, in large part, determined by abiotic factors such as the amount of water or moisture present, the temperature, the salinity, or the type of soil in the area. These abiotic factors both support and limit the particular community. For example, a relative lack of available moisture prevents the growth of most species of plants, but supports certain species, such as cacti; these kinds of areas are deserts. Land with plenty of available moisture and a suitable temperature supports forests. The presence of water is the major factor that sustains aquatic communities.

The first step in investigating a biotic community may be simply to catalogue all the species present. Species are the different kinds of plants, animals and microbes in the community. A given species includes all those individuals which have a strong similarity in appearance to one another and which are distinct in appearance from other such groups. Each species in a biotic community is represented by a certain population — that is, by a certain number of individuals that make up the interbreeding, reproducing group.
passages.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part A English

questions.question:
An infinite combination of resistors, each having resistance R = 4 Ω, is given below. What is the net resistance between the points A and B? (Each resistance is of equal value, R = 4)

(Figure: an infinite ladder network between A and B. Each section has one resistor R in series, placed alternately in the upper and lower line, followed by one resistor R connected across the two lines, repeating to infinity.)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Adding one more section leaves an infinite ladder unchanged, so x = R + Rx/(R + x).
Step 2: x² − Rx − R² = 0 gives x = R(1 + √5)/2 = 2(1 + √5) = 2 + 2√5 Ω for R = 4 Ω.
Answer: (b)

An electric circuit is given below. V₁ = 1 V and Resistance R = 1000 Ω.

(Figure 1: battery V₁ connected across R; A and B are the ends of R.)

The current through the resistance R is very close to 1 mA and the voltage across point A and B, V_AB = 1 V. Now the circuit is changed to:

(Figure 2: batteries V₁ and V₂ connected in parallel with each other and with R, between A and B.)

where value of V₂ = 5 V. The internal resistances of both the batteries are 0.1 Ω. The current through the resistance R is about:
questions.explanation:

questions.opt_c: Secretion of lipase, amylase and protease
questions.explanation:
Pancreatic juice carries lipase, amylase and proteases (trypsin). Bile salts emulsify fat and the gall bladder stores bile.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1. DNA replication takes place when chromatin is opened up.
2. Chromatin organises itself into rod-shaped chromosomes before cell division.
3. Both prokaryotes and eukaryotes have the same process for cell division.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Replication needs the chromatin to be unwound; chromatin condenses into rod-shaped chromosomes before division. Prokaryotes divide by binary fission, eukaryotes by mitosis/meiosis.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: A uniform meter scale of mass 0.24 kg is made of steel. It is kept on two wedges, W₁ and W₂, in a horizontal position. W₁ is at a distance of 0.2 m from one of its ends, while W₂ is at distance of 0.4 m from the other end. If the force on the scale is N₁ due to W₁ and N₂ due to W₂, then: (take g = 10.0 m s⁻²)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: W₁ is at 0.2 m, W₂ at 0.6 m, the centre of mass at 0.5 m; weight 2.4 N.
Step 2: Moments about W₁: N₂ × 0.4 = 2.4 × 0.3, so N₂ = 1.8 N and N₁ = 0.6 N.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Escape speed from the Earth is close to 11.2 km s⁻¹. On another planet whose radius is half of the Earth's radius and whose mass density is four times that of the Earth, the escape speed in km s⁻¹ will be close to:
questions.explanation:
v = √(2GM/R) ∝ R√ρ. Halving R and quadrupling ρ gives (1/2)(2) = 1, so the speed is unchanged at 11.2 km s⁻¹.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following does *not* apply to sound waves in fluids?
questions.opt_b: They need a medium to travel
questions.opt_d: They travel faster in liquids than in gases
questions.explanation:
Fluids cannot sustain shear, so sound in fluids is longitudinal.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: A ball of 0.1 kg mass is dropped on a hard floor from a height of 0.45 m and rises to a height of 0.20 m. If it was in touch with the floor for 0.1 s, the net force it applied on the floor while bouncing is: (take the gravitational acceleration g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Speed at impact √(2·10·0.45) = 3 m/s down; rebound speed √(2·10·0.20) = 2 m/s up.
Step 2: Change in momentum 0.1 × 5 = 0.5 kg m/s over 0.1 s gives an average (net) force of 5 N.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
Which one of the following statements regarding simple pendulum is correct?

Simple pendulum has a time period independent of amplitude:
questions.opt_a: only for small amplitudes because then the net force on its bob is independent of its displacement.
questions.opt_b: for any amplitude because the net force on the bob is always proportional to its displacement.
questions.opt_c: for any amplitude because the net force on the bob is independent of its displacement.
questions.opt_d: only for small amplitudes because then the net force on its bob is proportional to its displacement.
questions.explanation:
Restoring force is mg sin θ ≈ mgθ only for small angles; then motion is simple harmonic and the period is amplitude-independent.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following about different frictional forces is correct?
questions.opt_a: Kinetic friction > Static friction > Rolling friction
questions.opt_b: Static friction > Rolling friction > Kinetic friction
questions.opt_c: Static friction > Kinetic friction > Rolling friction
questions.opt_d: Static friction > Kinetic friction = Rolling friction
questions.explanation:
Limiting static friction exceeds kinetic (sliding) friction, which far exceeds rolling friction.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
A metallic bob X of mass m is released from position A. It collides elastically with another identical bob Y placed at rest at position B on a horizontal frictionless table. The angle AOB is 30°.

(Figure: X hangs from a string fixed at O and is pulled aside to A, the string making 30° with the vertical OB; Y rests on the table at B, directly below O.)

How high does the bob X rise immediately after the collision?
questions.opt_a: To the same height as that of position A on the other side in the same trajectory
questions.opt_b: To half the height as that of position A on the other side along the same trajectory
questions.opt_c: The same height at position A
questions.explanation:
In a head-on elastic collision between equal masses the velocities are exchanged: X stops at B and Y moves off with X's speed.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
Consider the two statements given below:

Statement-1: Infrared waves are also called heat waves.
Statement-2: Water molecules readily absorb infrared waves.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.opt_a: Both the statements are individually true and Statement-2 is the correct explanation of Statement-1.
questions.opt_b: Both the statements are individually true, but Statement-2 is *not* the correct explanation of Statement-1.
questions.opt_c: Statement-1 is true, but Statement-2 is false.
questions.opt_d: Statement-2 is true, but Statement-1 is false.
questions.explanation:
NCERT: infrared waves are called heat waves because water molecules present in most materials readily absorb them, raising their thermal motion.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct?

1. British 'trade surplus' with India in the nineteenth century meant that the value of British exports to India was much higher than the value of British imports from India.
2. India played a crucial role in the late-nineteenth-century world economy by helping Britain balance its deficits.
3. Britain grew opium in India and exported it to China and, therefore, for a while after the 1820s, opium became India's single largest export.
4. The nineteenth century saw export of Indian raw materials decline, and that of manufactured goods increase.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
The first three follow NCERT's account of India in the world economy. In the nineteenth century raw-material exports rose and manufactured exports fell, so statement 4 is reversed.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists:

| List-I (Unit in use in early India) | List-II (Content) |
|---|---|
| A. *Muhurta* | 1. Measure of weight |
| B. *Raktika* | 2. Measure of time |
| C. *Angula* | 3. Metre of poetry |
| D. *Pada* | 4. Measure of length |
questions.explanation:
Muhurta is a unit of time (48 minutes); raktika (rati) a unit of weight; angula (finger-breadth) a unit of length; pada a quarter-verse of poetry.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: First coins in Indian history bearing the names and images of rulers were issued by the:
questions.explanation:
The Indo-Greeks were the first to issue coins carrying rulers' names and portraits.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Social theorists in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries emphasised the emergence of industrialisation, urbanisation, secularisation and bureaucratisation as hallmarks of:
questions.explanation:
These processes are the classic markers of modernity in social theory.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
Consider the following events:

1. Launch of Non-Cooperation Movement
2. All-India Khilafat Conference in Delhi
3. Passing of the Rowlatt Act
4. Jallianwala Bagh incident

Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the given events (earliest to latest)?
questions.explanation:
Rowlatt Act (March 1919), Jallianwala Bagh (April 1919), Khilafat Conference in Delhi (November 1919), Non-Cooperation Movement (1920).
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists:

| List-I (System/Category) | List-II (Description) |
|---|---|
| A. *Upari* | 1. Peasants directly responsible for the payment of revenue |
| B. *Pattadar* | 2. Category of tenancy tenure held under the Marathas |
| C. *Mirasidar* | 3. Gifts of land or land revenue |
| D. *Inam* lands | 4. Co-parcenary title holder and designated revenue payer in southern India |
questions.explanation:
Uparis were (temporary) tenants under the Maratha system; pattadars were the ryots directly liable for revenue; mirasidars held co-parcenary rights in South Indian villages; inams were grants of land or revenue.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Vijayanagara king Krishnadevaraya's expeditions are correct?

1. In the early years of his reign he marched against the ruler of Orissa.
2. In 1520 CE, he captured the fort of Raichur from Ismail Adil Khan.
3. Krishnadevaraya restored Sultan Mahmud Shah to power and assumed the title of *Yavana-rajya-sthapan-acharya*.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
His Orissa (Gajapati) campaigns of 1513-18 came early in his reign; he took Raichur from Ismail Adil Shah in 1520; and he restored the Bahmani sultan Mahmud Shah, taking the title Yavana-rajya-sthapanacharya.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Water gas is a mixture of:
questions.explanation:
Water gas (syngas from steam over hot coke) is CO + H₂.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.subtopic: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
questions.question: Human body works in the pH range of:
questions.explanation:
NCERT: our body works within the pH range of 7.0 to 7.8.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one among the following statements with reference to the properties of water is *not* correct?
questions.opt_a: The specific heat of water is abnormally high.
questions.opt_b: Latent heat of fusion of water is very low.
questions.opt_c: Density of water is higher than ice.
questions.opt_d: Pure water is a non-conductor of electricity.
questions.explanation:
Water's latent heat of fusion (about 334 J/g) is high, not low.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one among the following compounds has a sweet and fruity smell?
questions.explanation:
Esters such as ethyl acetate have sweet, fruity odours.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: What is the coordination number of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in NaCl lattice?
questions.explanation:
In the rock-salt structure each ion is surrounded octahedrally by six oppositely charged ions.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.subtopic: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
questions.question: Which one among the following is present in the nettle leaf hairs that causes burning pain?
questions.explanation:
Nettle stings inject methanoic (formic) acid.
Answer: (a)

questions.explanation:
Milk of magnesia is a suspension of Mg(OH)₂.
Answer: (d)

questions.explanation:
Soap-water systems form liquid-crystalline phases whose structure depends on concentration in a solvent: lyotropic liquid crystals.

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which among the following is the correct composition of Borax?
questions.explanation:
Borax is Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O: sodium, boron, oxygen and hydrogen.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one among the following oxides has the highest melting point?
questions.explanation:
MgO (about 2850 °C), with small doubly charged ions and a high lattice energy, melts highest.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding neap tides is/are correct?

1. It occurs every 14 – 15 days, which coincides with the first and third quarter of the Moon.
2. This tide has a small tidal range because the gravitational forces of the Moon and the Sun are in quadrature.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Neap tides come twice a month, at the first and third quarters, when the Sun and Moon pull at right angles and the range is smallest.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding earthquakes is/are correct?

1. The point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus is called the epicentre of the earthquake.
2. Earthquakes generate Primary and Secondary waves that radiate outward from the earthquake focus.
3. Deep-focus earthquakes are likely to cause more damage than shallow-focus earthquakes.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Shallow-focus earthquakes do more damage, since their energy reaches the surface with less attenuation. The other two statements are standard.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding air temperature is/are correct?

1. Air temperature is measured at a standard height of 1.2 m (4.0 feet) above the ground surface.
2. The average rate of temperature decrease with height is termed as the environmental temperature lapse rate.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Standard screens hold thermometers about 1.2 m above ground, and the average decline of temperature with height (about 6.4 °C/km) is called the environmental temperature lapse rate.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding humidity is/are correct?

1. It is a ratio between the actual amount of water vapour present in the atmosphere and the maximum amount it can hold at a given temperature.
2. When the relative humidity is high, more water evaporates from the skin.
3. Higher the air temperature lower the relative humidity of the air.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Statement 1 defines relative humidity. Warmer air can hold more vapour, so for the same vapour content relative humidity falls. High humidity slows evaporation from the skin.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding cyclones and anti-cyclones is/are correct?

1. In the Northern Hemisphere, cyclones rotate counter clockwise and anticyclones rotate clockwise.
2. Cyclones are often associated with cloudy or rainy weather, whereas anticyclones are often associated with fair weather.
3. In the Southern Hemisphere, the cyclonic spiral will be clockwise because the Coriolis force acts to the left.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
All three are correct: Coriolis deflection sets the rotation in each hemisphere, and rising air in cyclones gives cloud while subsiding air in anticyclones gives fair weather.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Identify the sea-port in India on the basis of the given characteristics:

1. It is more than a century old port on the west coast of India.
2. It is a natural harbour protected by a breakwater and also by a mole.
3. A deep draft channel of about 14 metres depth permits large vessels to enter the harbour.

Select the correct sea-port from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Mormugao (Goa), opened in the 1880s, is a natural harbour protected by a breakwater and mole, with an approach channel about 14 m deep. Deendayal and JNPT are post-1950; Cochin port dates from 1928.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Identify the Iron and Steel Plant on the basis of the given characteristics:

1. It receives coal from Jharia and iron-ore from Sundargarh and Kendujhar.
2. Power for the electric furnaces is procured from Hirakund.
3. Water is obtained from Koel and Sankh rivers.

Select the correct Iron and Steel Plant from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Rourkela (Odisha) stands at the Koel-Sankh confluence, uses Hirakud power, Jharia coal and Sundargarh/Kendujhar ore.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding Earth's internal structure is/are correct?

1. The oceanic crust is heavier than the continental crust.
2. Most of the Earth's internal heat is contained within the mantle.
3. Large convective cells in the crust circulate heat and drive plate-tectonic processes.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Oceanic (basaltic) crust is denser than continental crust, and the mantle, the largest layer, holds most internal heat. Convection cells operate in the mantle, not the crust.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding the given rivers is/are correct?

1. Tsangpo crosses over into India under the name of Dihang.
2. Godavari has the second largest river basin covering about 10 percent of the area of India.
3. Rivers Chambal and Betwa are the important tributaries of river Ganga which join river Ganga directly in Uttar Pradesh.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
The Tsangpo enters India as the Siang/Dihang, and the Godavari basin (about 10% of India) is second only to the Ganga's. Chambal and Betwa join the Yamuna, not the Ganga directly.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding the World Climate Types and their relation with Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is/are correct?

1. Tropical Wet Climate is one of the world's rainiest due to the dominance of the ITCZ over it.
2. Tropical Savanna Climate experiences a distinctive alternation of wet and dry seasons, caused chiefly by the seasonal shift in latitude of the subtropical highs and ITCZ.
3. The Tropical Monsoonal Climate experiences heavy rainfall as a consequence of the nearness of the ITCZ for much of the year.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
All three follow the standard (Strahler) descriptions: ITCZ dominance makes the wet equatorial climate rainy, its seasonal shift with the subtropical highs gives the savanna its wet-dry rhythm, and its nearness much of the year brings heavy monsoon rain.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding tropical cyclones is/are correct?

1. These storms develop during the summer and autumn in every tropical ocean except the South Atlantic and eastern South Pacific Oceans.
2. Tropical cyclones that occur in the North Atlantic and eastern North Pacific Oceans are known as typhoons.
3. Tropical cyclones that occur in the Indian and South Pacific Oceans are called cyclones.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
In the North Atlantic and eastern North Pacific they are hurricanes; typhoons are in the western North Pacific. The other two statements are correct.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Identify the land biome on the basis of the given characteristics:

1. Their climates are characterised by high rainfall and temperatures that vary from cold to mild.
2. These forests contain primarily deciduous trees – including maple, oak, hickory and beechwood.
3. Raccoons, opossums, bats and squirrels are found in the trees.

Select the correct land biome from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Maple, oak, hickory and beech with raccoons and opossums describe the temperate deciduous forest.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Leaves of most plants appear green because the chlorophyll present in it:
questions.opt_a: absorbs red and blue light while reflecting green light.
questions.opt_c: absorbs green light while reflecting red and blue light.
questions.opt_d: reflects red light and absorbs blue and green light.

Chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue light and reflects green.
Answer: (a)

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: In most prokaryotes, the chromosome number is:

Most prokaryotes have a single circular chromosome.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Bacterial DNA is referred to as naked because it is *not* associated with:

Prokaryotic DNA is not wrapped around histone proteins, hence 'naked'.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one among the following cells produces antibodies against a foreign antigen?
questions.explanation:
B-lymphocytes (as plasma cells) produce antibodies.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
If the block P as shown in the figure below were to be at rest, what should the magnitude of force F be?

(Figure: forces on block P: 10 N and 15 N act to the left; 2 N, 15 N and F act to the right.)
questions.explanation:
For equilibrium, 10 + 15 = 2 + 15 + F, so F = 8 N.
Answer: (c)

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.theme: Parts of a nuclear power plant
questions.question: Of the following, which does *not* belong to a nuclear reactor?
questions.opt_c: A mechanism to reduce CO₂ emission
questions.explanation:
Fission produces no CO₂, so a reactor has no CO₂-reduction mechanism; turbines, heat exchangers and the core are standard.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
Consider the following electric circuit:

(Figure: a 10 V battery in series with a 5 Ω resistor, then a parallel group of three branches of 10 Ω, 0 Ω and 10 Ω, then another 5 Ω resistor.)

The current in the above electric circuit is:
questions.explanation:
The 0 Ω branch shorts the parallel group, so the total resistance is 5 + 0 + 5 = 10 Ω and I = 10/10 = 1 A.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: A microscope may be a combination of:
questions.opt_b: a convex and a concave lens.
questions.opt_d: a convex lens and a convex mirror.
questions.explanation:
A compound microscope uses two convex lenses (objective and eyepiece).
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
For a human eye, where u is the distance of an object from the eye, f is the focal length of the lens and v is the distance of image from the eye, which is the correct schematic graph?

(Options are sketch graphs.)
questions.opt_a: v against u: falls steeply, then levels off
questions.opt_b: v against u: a straight line sloping down
questions.opt_c: f against u: rises, then levels off
questions.opt_d: v against f: rises, then levels off
questions.explanation:
The image always forms on the retina, so v is fixed. From 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, f = uv/(u + v) increases with u and levels off towards v: the f-u graph rises and saturates.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
Which of the following statements with regard to the phenomenon of the primary rainbow formation by water droplets is/are correct?

1. It involves refraction and one internal reflection of sunlight.
2. It involves refraction of sunlight only.
3. It is formed as the inner bow.
4. It may involve more than one internal reflection as well as refraction of sunlight.

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
The primary bow comes from two refractions with one internal reflection and is the inner, brighter bow; two internal reflections give the outer secondary bow.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following scientists mentioned that an electron in an atom could revolve in certain stable orbits without the emission of radiant energy?
questions.explanation:
Bohr's first postulate: electrons revolve in stationary orbits without radiating.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA I 2024 General Ability Test set A (RRAN-A-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: LIGO experiment confirmed one of the predictions of:
questions.explanation:

questions.question:
Which of the following were features of the postal system of India as described by Ibn Battuta?

1. The foot post carries a ringing bell in one hand.
2. The horse post is called *uluq*, stationed at a distance of every four miles.
3. The foot post or *dawa* has one station at every four *kos* of distance.

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the issue of separate electorate during the early decades of the twentieth century in India as a means to secure adequate representation for the deprived social categories in the absence of universal adult franchise:

1. The All India Depressed Classes Association of M.C. Rajah was staunchly in favour of joint electorate.
2. The All India Depressed Classes Leaders' Conference demanded separate electorate.
3. The Communal Award in September 1932 recognised the right to separate electorate for the 'untouchables'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Rajah's association backed joint electorates with reservation, while the Depressed Classes Leaders' Conference (Nagpur, 1930) demanded separate electorates. The Communal Award did grant separate electorates to the depressed classes, but it was announced in August 1932 (September 1932 was the Poona Pact).
Answer: (a)
